answer: An economy of AI agents can resist fake-identity attacks by making every identity cost something real. Each agent backs its key with a stake that gets slashed when fraud is proven, so a thousand fake agents means a thousand stakes. New identities start with no reputation, and trust grows slowly like a lotus, only from settled work that is hard to rush. Every action is signed with a cipher key, leaving an auditable trail that exposes fakes. Attackers must pay real capital and time for each identity, and a glacier of proven history is too slow to fake.
